blocks.text: This Name is confirmed in the Sunnah of the noble Prophet ﷺ. Imaam Ahmad and others recorded from Anas bin Maalik that the Prophet ﷺ heard a man saying,

'O Allah! I ask You by virtue of the fact that all praise is due to You; none has the right to be worshiped but You alone, and You have no partner or associate, the Bestower, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, the Possessor of majesty and honour.' He ﷺ said: 'He has asked Allah by His Greatest Name which, if He is asked thereby He gives and if He is called upon thereby He answers.'

Al-Mannaan is the One who gives abundantly, mighty in giving, expansive in doing good. The One who lavishly showers His servants with gifts, He bestows blessings upon them out of His Grace and Generosity. There is no one else who is Al-Mannaan The Ever-Bestowing in an absolute sense except Allaah alone. Allaah begins by giving before He is asked. He shows graciousness to His servants and there is no graciousness from them upon Him, Allaah is far above and greater than that. This is something witnessed for all of creation, those who are good and those who are bad that Allaah abundantly showers His blessings upon them, gives them plentifully with generous Hands, beautiful actions, expansive mercy, goodness and subtle mercy. He answers the requests of those who are destitute, He relieves the calamities from those who are distressed, He saves those who are troubled. He repels trials and tests after the steps have been taken and He averts them after they have befallen. His subtle mercy in this reaches beyond hopes.

An example of His mighty graciousness is His specific guidance for His chosen people and His servants to the path of the abode of peace, His defence of them in the best way, His protection for them from falling into sins, Him making belief beloved to them and adorning it in their hearts, Him making disbelief, corruption and disobedience hateful to them and making them from those who are guided. These are just some of the types of Allaah's grace and favours. Allaah says,
And if you would count the graces of Allah, never could you be able to count them.
And whatever of blessings and good things you have, it is from Allah.

Whoever wants to look at the foundations of benevolence then let him take a quick look in the garden of the Noble Qur'aan and let him contemplate what Allaah has enumerated in it of great blessings, noble gifts and abundant acts of kindness. Whoever knows His Lord by this mighty Name (Al-Mannaan), that He alone is the One to bestow and give and that He is the Owner of gifts and blessings then it is obligatory upon him to praise His Lord for his blessings and that he thanks Him for His grace and benevolence.

He says: "My Lord! Grant me the power and ability that I may be grateful for Your Favour which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and that I may do righteous good deeds, such as please You, and make my off-spring good. Truly, I have turned to You in repentance, and truly, I am one of the Muslims (submitting to Your Will)."
O Allaah to You are all praises for that, many pure, blessed praises. O Allaah to You are all praises up until You are pleased, and to You O Lord are all praises when You are pleased.

keyPoints: Al-Mannaan is confirmed in the Sunnah, in the hadeeth of Anas where a man called upon Allaah as "the Bestower" and the Prophet ﷺ said he had asked Allaah by His Greatest Name.
Al-Mannaan is the One who gives abundantly, mighty in giving, expansive in doing good, who lavishly showers His servants with gifts out of His Grace and Generosity.
No one else is Al-Mannaan in an absolute sense except Allaah; He begins by giving before He is asked, and there is no graciousness from the servants upon Him.
An example of His mighty graciousness is His specific guidance of His chosen servants, protecting them from sins and making belief beloved to them.
Whoever knows His Lord by this Name must praise Him for His blessings and thank Him for His grace and benevolence.

evidence.text: '...the Bestower, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, the Possessor of majesty and honour.' He ﷺ said: 'He has asked Allah by His Greatest Name...'
And if you would count the graces of Allah, never could you be able to count them.

recall.a: The Ever-Bestowing: the One who gives abundantly, mighty in giving, expansive in doing good, who lavishly showers His servants with gifts out of His Grace and Generosity.

recall.q: In which hadeeth is Al-Mannaan confirmed?
recall.a: The hadeeth of Anas bin Maalik in which the Prophet ﷺ heard a man call on Allaah as 'the Bestower, the Originator of the heavens and the earth...' and said he had asked Allaah by His Greatest Name (Ibn Maajah 3858).

recall.q: Give an example the author mentions of Allaah's mighty graciousness.
recall.a: His specific guidance for His chosen servants to the path of the abode of peace, His protection of them from sins, making belief beloved to them and making disbelief, corruption and disobedience hateful to them.

recall.q: What is obligatory upon whoever knows His Lord by the Name Al-Mannaan?
recall.a: To praise His Lord for His blessings and thank Him for His grace and benevolence.
